title: Delhi Deploys 26,000 Central Forces Ahead of CJP's October 10 Jantar Mantar Protest
excerpt: About 11,000 additional CAPF personnel, taking total central force presence to 26,000, will guard the capital through October 12 as the Cockroach Janta Party plans a Jantar Mantar protest demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
body:
• Delhi is deploying roughly 11,000 additional CAPF personnel ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's planned protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, taking the total central force presence in the capital to about 26,000, according to reports. Some 20,000 Delhi Police personnel are also expected on the streets.
  • The additional forces stay in place at least through October 12. Delhi Police has denied permission for the gathering and warned that any illegal assembly will face legal action.
  • CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke is demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and has vowed the group will not leave until Kumar steps down.
  • If you are in Delhi this weekend: expect barricades and checks across central Delhi through Monday, October 12. Avoid Jantar Mantar and surrounding areas; Section 163 is in effect, and police say illegal gatherings can carry long-term legal consequences.

Delhi is bracing for one of its largest security deployments of the year. About 11,000 additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel are being deployed across the national capital ahead of a planned protest at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, October 10, taking the total central force presence in the city to roughly 26,000, reported Hindustan Times, citing sources. NDTV reported that around 20,000 Delhi Police personnel are also expected to be deployed during the demonstration. The extra forces will remain in the capital at least until October 12.

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, has called for thousands of supporters to converge at Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Dipke has said his group will not leave the protest site until Kumar steps down, and warned that if police stop marchers on the way, "the place where they are stopped will become their Jantar Mantar."

Permission denied, Section 163 in force

Delhi Police has not granted permission for the gathering. Officials have clarified that Section 163 is in effect, which means protests are not permitted at Jantar Mantar or anywhere else without approval, and any gathering will be treated as illegal.

"Section 163 is in effect, meaning protests are not permitted — neither at Jantar Mantar nor anywhere else. Any gathering will be considered illegal, and we would be compelled to take necessary legal action against it."

— Shrishti Pandey, DCP, Delhi Police

DCP Shrishti Pandey urged residents not to participate in illegal gatherings, warning of long-term legal consequences. Separately, security has been strengthened at the CEC's home and office, with The Hindu reporting additional forces deployed around Gyanesh Kumar following the Z+ security upgrade.

Background: a pressure group's record of disruption

The CJP is a new-style pressure outfit that has built its profile through confrontation. On October 2, it staged a protest at Shivaji Park in Mumbai over the same SIR demands even though police had denied permission, drawing thousands of young supporters. Earlier in July, the group led a protest against then-Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, who subsequently resigned. Following the Mumbai protest, the CJP issued a "Chalo Delhi" call, mobilizing workers from across the country for October 10.

The agitation runs parallel to the INDIA bloc's ongoing campaign against the CEC over the same SIR issue. Hundreds of opposition leaders and workers were detained after a march toward the Election Commission and an eight-hour sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan, and INDIA bloc MPs again marched toward Jantar Mantar this week.

The Election Commission has pushed back, saying its decisions — including those related to the SIR exercise — were taken unanimously, and has dismissed the rigging allegations.

Why it matters

The scale of the deployment signals how seriously the government is taking the threat of disruption. Pulling forces from Jammu and Kashmir and anti-Naxal operations, as ThePrint reported, underscores both the seriousness of the preparations and the political cost of moving troops from active theaters.

What's next

All eyes are on Saturday. With permission denied and tens of thousands of personnel on the streets, the question is whether CJP supporters will attempt to breach barricades — as they did in Mumbai — or settle for a symbolic gathering. Diaspora readers with family in Delhi or travel plans to the capital this weekend should check with local contacts before heading into central Delhi; barricading at Jantar Mantar, Connaught Place and nearby metro stations is likely through Monday.
